newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures barely changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures barely changed in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were barely changed in very quiet dealings at the start of a holiday-shortened session.
"Nobody is doing anything," said one T-bond futures trader on the floor of the Chicago Board of Trade, noting that the biggest orders being executed in the pit were 50-lots.
One firm, "tried to sell 500 and people started laughing," said another T-bond floor broker at a large U.S. bank.
Some traders also said the day's range in the bond contract may already be set.
Resistance in the March T-bond is near 113-20/32 to 113-21/32, which is Monday's high and the high from last Friday, respectively. Support is evident near the three-day moving average at 113-10/32.

Traders said there was little reaction to a rise of 1.3 percent in chain store sales the week ended December 21 in the BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index. A rise of 1.3 percent had been expected.
Interest rate futures at CBOT close at 1210 CST/1810 GMT today, while debt futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange finish at 1200 CST/1800 CST for the Christmas holiday.
Exchanges are closed Wednesday all day for Christmas.

At 0837 CST, March T-bond futures were off 2/32 point at 113-12/32, 10-year T-notes were unchanged at 109-22/32 and muni-bonds were 3/32 lower at 116-05/32. March IMM T-bills were two basis points higher at 94.97 and Eurodollars were one point lower at 94.44.
